text:
izzy: Heads-up — after canary v3 rollout we got a burst of reconnects and token churn. Console shows ~4k reconnects in a 5m window and a small billing spike.

sam: Ugh. Any obvious error codes in the proxy or ws logs? link to the realtime dashboard: https://console/realtime (short link)

izzy: Pasting a trimmed log sample: 
```
proxy-1 | 2026-03-21T14:02:12Z INFO connection closed 204 missing-session-header tenant=acme
proxy-1 | 2026-03-21T14:02:12Z DEBUG removed resume-token id=abc123 origin=ws
client | 2026-03-21T14:02:12Z INFO reconnect attempt=1 backoff=120ms
```

maya: That 204 path looks familiar — proxy treats 204 as terminal and releases session immediately. If client retries before our lease window expires we lose sticky routing and end up in a new session (double-charge / extra reconnects).

sam: Are we sampling session-tombstone telemetry? I want to see how often this pattern happens across tenants.

taylor: Current sampling for session tombstones is 0.5%. We won't get good signal for spikes. I propose bumping to 5% for 30m while we debug. @ops-bot can you do that?

ops-bot: sampling.adjust called by taylor: metric=session_tombstone.sample_rate -> 0.05 ; duration=30m ; roll=true

izzy: After bump we see the same 204->immediate-release pattern across a few shards. Also noticed resume-token header stripped by proxy when upstream returned 204 on the keepalive path.

sam: Two independent issues then: (A) treating 204 as terminal; (B) telemetry undersampling. Fix order: bump sampling (done), then quick proxy change. Proposed proxy behavior: if response is 204 but Resume-Id header present, treat as transient (do not delete resume token), and start a short grace timer (default 5s) before lease claim. Thoughts?

maya: Agree. We need console/route UX to surface "sticky fallback reason" when a session migrates so SREs can correlate with tenant quota/edge flaps. Add a small telemetry tag like sticky.fallback_reason=proxy_204 to route events.

taylor: Also add a sampling-exempt path: when sticky.fallback_reason present, always emit a full trace (no sample). That'll give us deterministic traces for these incidents.

dev-console: Noted. I can add a UI column and a drilldown link to the route timeline. Will follow the telemetry tag schema.

sam: Can we make the proxy change minimal and safe? e.g., three small steps: 1) stop deleting resume-token on proxy-204, 2) start 5s grace timer, 3) add feature flag for canary. Backwards compat preserved.

izzy: I can test step 1 on canary shard. Will run with increased sampling.

ops-bot: canary patch deploy queued: proxy/patch-204-grace ttl=5s flag=proxy.keep_resume_on_204.canary

taylor: I'll open a tiny PR for the telemetry tag + sample-exempt logic. Requesting review from @maya and @sam.

izzy: Created incident note and issue: https://issues/4521 — brief: "proxy 204 prematurely releases sticky session -> reconnect churn". I attached logs and dashboard snapshot.

sam: Thanks. If the canary patch holds for 1h with no extra reconnects we can roll. Also add a console alert rule that surfaces sudden reconnect rate deltas > 200% baseline in 5m windows. Right now the dashboard smoothing hid the spike.

maya: Agreed — I'll add the alert and the UI column for fallback reason.

dev-console: Alert rule created: reconnect_rate.delta_5m > 2x baseline -> page on-call. Added drill link to timeline with sticky.fallback_reason tag.

taylor: Follow-ups: PR+tests for proxy behavior, console UI change, keep sampling for 2h then revert to 0.5% unless we see recurrence.

izzy: Canary looks stable after 22m, reconnects dropped to baseline. Leaving sampling at 5% for now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
